Assessment
37-year-old female (MRN SYN-6411760) with prediabetes and 12-year history of combined oral contraceptive use (levonorgestrel 0.15 mg / ethinyl estradiol 0.03 mg daily since 2012) evaluated for intermittent right upper quadrant discomfort. Baseline liver tests (2024-05-06) are normal (ALT 24 U/L, AST 22 U/L, ALP 71 U/L, total bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL, albumin 4.3 g/dL, platelets 268 K/uL) and renal function is normal (Cr 0.7 mg/dL). No history of cirrhosis, viral hepatitis (HBV/HCV negative), or heavy alcohol use.

1. Indeterminate Solid Hepatic Lesion (4.8 x 4.1 cm in segment 6): Abdominal ultrasound (2024-05-24) shows a well-circumscribed 4.8 x 4.1 cm solid, mildly hyperechoic lesion with internal vascularity on color Doppler in a non-cirrhotic liver. Differential diagnosis in a reproductive-age woman on long-term estrogen-containing oral contraceptives includes hepatocellular adenoma (HCA), focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH), and atypical hemangioma. Because the lesion approaches 5 cm and is strongly associated with exogenous estrogen exposure, HCA must be excluded or confirmed given the risk of hemorrhage/rupture and malignant transformation.
